n: The Psalms open with a doorway psalm describing two paths. The happy person doesn’t drift into evil step by step — walking with, then standing with, then sitting with those who mock God.

f.g: Hebrew ’ashre — “happy” or “how fortunate”; the same idea as the Beatitudes.

f.w: sitteth in the seat of the scornful
f.g: Walking, standing, then sitting — a progression showing how gradually sin can settle in.

n: Instead, this person loves God’s teaching and thinks about it constantly. The positive habit, not just avoiding evil, is what shapes him.

f.g: Hebrew torah — instruction or teaching, not only rules.

n: Such a person is like a tree planted beside irrigation channels: it bears fruit at the right time, its leaves stay green, and it thrives.

f.w: a tree planted by the rivers of water

f.g: Irrigation channels — the tree was deliberately planted by a reliable water source.

n: The wicked are the opposite — like chaff, the light husks blown away when grain is tossed in the wind at harvest. They have no weight or root.

f.g: Worthless husks separated from grain by winnowing.

n: So the wicked will not stand firm at the judgment, nor belong in the gathering of the righteous.

f.w: shall not stand in the judgment

n: The Lord knows — personally watches over — the path of the righteous, while the path of the wicked leads to ruin.

f.g: In Hebrew, “know” implies close, caring relationship.
